test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Why/how did the word, which had originally been offensive, become unoffensive suddenly?

options.text: Because of people’s age and norms
Because of the control by the Censor Board
Because of changed sensitivity of American culture

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explains that the word, which was originally offensive, became unoffensive due to the changed sensitivities of American culture.
 
• The change in cultural sensitivities allowed for the amendment of the Motion Picture Production Code, which led to the word being considered unoffensive at the time of the movie's release.
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate reason for the word becoming unoffensive is the changed sensitivity of American culture, making Option 3 the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Because of people’s age and norms" **and **"Because of the control by the Censor Board"** are not directly related to the change in perception of the word 'damn' mentioned in the passage.
 
• **"Because of conventions" **is also not the direct reason as the passage refers to a shift in cultural sensitivity, not conventions.
